author: By_Tor2114
text: I think the tricky part is knowing when a swing is a reaction to a flag limit, or when a swing actually is a flag limit.

author: smimon
text:
By_Tor2114 wrote: I think the tricky part is knowing when a swing is a reaction to a flag limit, or when a swing actually is a flag limit.

You just need to look left (and possibly left again) and see if there is any obvious RBR or DBD that was formed after breaking a level, that price is reacting to. That is then the level that you look for the break of, not the swing itself. This way, you can avoid FOs, by being aware of where the actual edge of the important FL is. Sometimes you get a series of stacked FTRs all on top of a FL - this is then compression.

Sometimes the levels look insignificant, like the one on GU. But the market tells us it is important, because the last FTR into the top formed after bouncing from it. Therefore the break of this FL (also bearing in mind what we'd bounced from above) was significant.

Without the added information of bouncing from a HTF/big FTR/FL above, then it's harder to gauge the importance of a FL breaking. FL break without apparent reason for the break = no trade for me. I will only take the ones where I can clearly see a reason for the bounce and break.

Hope that helps.

Not sure what you mean? It's a continuation flag, so we're concerned with getting in long when the flag completes at the bottom. In this case, price hit demand, pole up, then smaller flag back down to fresh demand - this would have been the entry.

author: smimon
text:
My take on this one (was just looking at it myself) - price CP'd up into supply, broke down into CP, made a FTR, and continued. This is what we RT'd to - it was a good level to expect a reaction from on FTB. I'm starting to use M5/M15 a bit more now to spot these sort of levels, since what can just appear as a confusion of levels on M1, is clear on M5 when some of the "noise" is smoothed out.

If you're having trouble finding possible RT levels on M1, just try M5/M15, and see if it makes the picture clearer. Often, it gives us a clearer picture of where the large surges originated from. However, for checking whether important FLs have been engulfed, we always need to look on M1 for precision.

author: smimon
text:
Since I've been getting more consistent with my trading recently, I've also been getting more uptight. Pulling the trigger for the first trade of the day isn't so hard, but then if it wins, and I've already met my daily target, I just kind of freeze, and let opportunities pass me by, afraid to lose what I've gained.

I think I'll open another demo account, so I've got one "proper" one that I only use for concrete confirmed trades, and another practice one where I can take the slightly less certain entries (where I'm not 100% that I've read price correctly) that I still think have a good chance of playing out favourably, and continue to improve my learning in that way.
